I couldn’t sit through a full planning meeting; I’d keep getting up, pacing, checking emails, starting new ideas before finishing the last ones. I’m exhausted all the time, even when I actually sleep through the night. I keep replaying little mistakes—like mixing up seating charts or snapping at my assistant—and I can’t stop beating myself up over them. Getting out of bed felt like wading through cement. I kept thinking my work was terrible, that I was a fraud and a burden to everyone.

Then about a month ago it flipped. I suddenly had this burst of energy. I was sleeping maybe three hours a night and waking up wired, not tired at all. My mood would swing from feeling on top of the world to snapping at my husband over nothing, sometimes within the same hour. I jump at every little sound or movement; I’ll drop what I’m doing because a light flickers or someone walks by the window. Normally I’m pretty focused with delicate work, but this past month I’ve been too scattered and am making mistakes, so my boss asked me to take some time off.

Over the last few months, I feel like I’ve been swinging between two completely different versions of myself.

About three months ago, I went through roughly a month where I was “on” all the time. I’d wake up after a couple of hours of sleep feeling wired, like I didn’t need any more rest. My mood bounced around a lot—one minute I’d be buzzing, full of ideas for new business lines or redesigning my whole office, and the next I’d snap at my staff over tiny things. I couldn’t sit still in meetings; I’d pace, fiddle with samples, check my phone. I’d start five projects at once—new client pitches, a showroom revamp, reorganizing my apartment—and leave half of them half-done because my attention just jumped to the next thing. My mind wouldn’t shut off, especially at night; thoughts just kept looping and branching and I couldn’t slow them down. It started affecting the firm—missed deadlines, my team avoiding me.

Then, for the past two months, it’s like the bottom dropped out. I’ve been exhausted all the time, even simple things like answering emails feel draining. I’ve been dodging friends’ calls, cancelling dinners, barely seeing anyone outside of work. I keep getting these overwhelming, almost irrational feelings that I’m somehow to blame for anything that goes wrong—if a client’s project stalls, if a contractor has an accident, I feel like it’s my fault, like I’ve ruined everything, even when people tell me it doesn’t make sense. It’s been hard to keep the business running and to keep up any kind of personal life.

My mood would swing from feeling ecstatic and invincible to snapping at people over nothing within the same hour. I couldn’t sit still—pacing, reorganizing the office at 2 a.m., sketching three different projects at once. I barely slept, maybe two hours a night, and I didn’t feel tired at all, just wired. My mind wouldn’t shut up—thoughts racing so fast I couldn’t catch them. I’d start redesigning my entire showroom, then jump to planning a new branch, then rewriting contracts, without finishing anything. My team said I was talking a mile a minute and jumping topics so fast they couldn’t follow.  

Then, about six weeks ago, it all crashed. Now I can hardly drag myself out of bed. I avoid calls from clients and friends; I just don’t have it in me to deal with anyone. Walking from my bedroom to the kitchen feels exhausting. I’m convinced that a supplier’s bankruptcy last year was somehow my fault, and even random bad news on TV feels like I caused it. It’s gotten to the point where I’ve stopped going into the office.

I’ve always been the “too much” person. Even as a kid in grade school I couldn’t sit still, talked over everyone, blurted things out, stayed up late rearranging my room or sketching ideas, and I just never seemed to slow down like other kids. That’s pretty much continued my whole life, just… louder lately.

For as long as I can remember, my brain runs like twenty tabs open at once. My speech can get really fast because I’m trying to keep up with my thoughts, and I jump from one idea to the next. At work I’ll start designing a lobby, then suddenly I’m answering emails, then I’m halfway through a new concept board—nothing actually gets finished unless my team corrals me. Sitting through meetings is torture; I’m fidgeting, pacing, checking my phone. I hate “doing nothing.”

Sleep has never felt necessary. Even now, I’ll go on four or five hours for weeks, buzzing with ideas, and I don’t feel tired in the moment—just wired. Eventually I crash: I stop taking calls, ignore friends, and feel completely drained. In those down periods I get stuck thinking I’ve ruined people’s lives with small mistakes, like a client losing a contract because I sent one late email. I know it’s irrational, but it feels absolutely true when I’m in it.

About five months ago I went through this stretch, maybe two months, where I just felt like I was buzzing all the time. I couldn’t sit still between clients, I’d be pacing, cleaning, reorganizing colors, talking nonstop. I’d feel super on top of the world one minute, laughing and joking with everyone, and then the next I’d snap at a coworker over something tiny.  

I also started doing things I normally wouldn’t, like hooking up with guys I barely knew after going out, not really thinking about if it was safe. That’s not usually me, and afterward I’d feel kind of ashamed but during it I just felt like I had to keep going, like I needed that rush.

Then it sort of flipped. For the last three months I’ve been pulling away from my friends, ignoring group chats, making excuses not to go out. At work I stare at the polish wall forever because I can’t even pick a color to suggest. Even choosing what to wear in the morning feels like this huge decision.  

I wake up a lot in the middle of the night and just lie there, going over everything I’ve messed up. A few times I’ve thought really specifically about how I could end things—like where I’d do it and what I’d use. That scared me, but the thoughts keep coming back, and it’s getting harder to keep up my “I’m fine” act with clients.

I’d come into work buzzing, talking a mile a minute to clients, jumping from one idea to the next, starting new designs before I’d finished the last one. My thoughts were going so fast I could barely keep up. I hardly slept—maybe three hours a night—but I wasn’t tired at all. I’d pace around my apartment, reorganize everything at 3 a.m., scroll and text nonstop. 

My mood was all over the place: one minute I felt amazing, like I was unstoppable and extra flirty with everyone, and the next I’d snap at coworkers over tiny things. I even hooked up with a few guys I barely knew after work, which is really not like me, and it messed things up with some regular clients and my boss.

Then it crashed. For the last three months I’ve mostly stayed home when I’m not at the salon, ignoring friends’ messages. I wake up several times a night and just lie there, stuck in my head. Even simple stuff—picking an outfit, deciding what to eat—feels impossible. I’ve been thinking a lot about ending it, down to where I’d do it and how, and that scares me. It’s gotten hard to show up to work and actually care.

Even now at the salon, I’ll start a set of nails, get distracted by a design idea or my phone, and it’s hard to stay focused. I talk really fast with clients, and they sometimes say, “Slow down, girl.”

I’d wake up after three, four hours of sleep and feel more wired than after coffee, like my body just didn’t need rest. My thoughts were racing so fast I could barely keep up; I’d jump from redesigning our entire backyard to starting a side business to rearranging the whole office planting plan at 3 a.m. I talked nonstop, way too fast, and couldn’t sit still in meetings. I even hooked up with a coworker on a site visit—totally out of character and obviously a disaster for my marriage and work. My firm had to pull me from a couple of projects.

I sleep enough but wake up exhausted, like I haven’t rested at all. Picking what to wear or what to eat can paralyze me.
